findings.title: nil SubType still panics unmarshalVector instead of returning an error
findings.claim: A caller-built VectorType with nil SubType still panics unmarshalVector on the Scan goroutine instead of returning an error, via vectorElemMinSize(nil) hitting elemType.Type() or info.Zero() calling v.SubType.NewWithError() on a nil interface; reproduced with Unmarshal(VectorType{}, []byte{}, &a) where a is type any.

findings.title: Saturation branch of vectorElemMinSize (math.MaxInt32) has no test coverage
findings.claim: The return math.MaxInt32 branch that prevents the accumulator from wrapping under deeply nested peer-controlled Dimensions is untested; replacing it with return 1<<20 in a worktree left all vector tests green.

findings.title: 32-bit wrap/saturation cases cannot be executed on GOARCH=386
findings.claim: The 32-bit wrap cases in TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsUnfittableDimensions and the saturation arithmetic in marshal.go:1136-1137 cannot be executed on GOARCH=386 because dependent packages don't compile on 32-bit; verified only by inspection, and by inspection the arithmetic is safe.

findings.title: No test drives the allocation bound through the public Unmarshal entry point
findings.claim: No test exercises the bound via the public Unmarshal entry with variable-length fixed-Go-size elements (smallint/tinyint/date/time) or an array destination at exactly the minimum size; a manual probe passed, so this is coverage, not a defect.

findings.title: Memory-measurement test could be flaky from leaked goroutines allocating during…
findings.claim: TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsNestedCountBeforeAllocating measures process-wide runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc with a 128 KB budget and is not t.Parallel, so goroutines leaked by earlier tests in the package could allocate inside the measurement window and cause flakiness; no failure was observed in this run.

findings.title: Dimension bound misclassifies zero-length fixed custom types as variable-length
findings.claim: The dimension bound treats every unknown custom element type as variable-length with a 1-byte minimum, which is non-narrowing for a zero-length fixed type (EmptyType) that isVectorVariableLengthType already mis-classifies; described as pre-existing and out of scope, and not a realistic vector element.

findings.title: Recursion depth in vector-type helpers bounded only by short-string type-name length
findings.claim: Nested-vector recursion depth across vectorElemMinSize, isVectorVariableLengthType, and getCassandraLongType is bounded by the short-string custom type name length (allowing depth ~1500); this diff adds one more recursive walker of the same depth but does not change the exposure.

findings.title: Negative vint element length can cause element decode from nil data with nil error
findings.claim: For a variable-length element, elemSize = int(m) from readUnsignedVInt can go negative on 64-bit (m >= 2^63), and the element then decodes from nil data with a nil error; the new bound limits element count, not per-element lengths. Declared out of scope by the PR (#1106).
